data.title: Validate and enforce initial mapping prerequisites
data.when: Before executing any complex data transformation or object-to-object mapping where upstream dependencies are critical, particularly if previous runs failed due to unexpected input state.
procedure: Identify all required external service states or datasets that must be present for the mapping process (the 'expectations').
Implement explicit pre-checks to confirm these dependencies meet minimum structural and data quality requirements.
If any prerequisite check fails, halt execution immediately and report a specific dependency failure error, rather than allowing the mapping logic to proceed with corrupted or missing assumptions.
Ensure that all necessary reference data mappings are loaded/initialized *before* the primary transformation loop begins.
pitfalls: Relying on implicit state: Assuming that required data fields or services will be available when they are not, leading to runtime exceptions or silently incorrect output.
Failure to test boundary conditions: The skill might pass when simple cases run, but fail spectacularly when edge case mappings (e.g., null values in expected non-null fields) are encountered.
verification: The execution flow successfully passes the dependency checks without needing manual intervention or debugging of assumed state.
The final mapped output structure conforms to the schema and contains the correct data types, confirming that the inputs were validated correctly at the start.
